messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: submit variable via get to mirtcat
parts:
It's possible to define the item response stimuli using artibrary HTML code, or the HTML tags avilable in shiny and other packages. For example,

 # help(tags, package='shiny')
 options <- matrix(c("Strongly Disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly Agree"),
                   nrow = 3, ncol = 5, byrow = TRUE)
 shinyStems <- list(HTML('Building CATs with mirtCAT is difficult.'),
                div(HTML('mirtCAT requires a'), br(), HTML('substantial amount of coding.')),
                div(strong('I would use'), HTML('mirtCAT in my research.')))
 questions <- sapply(shinyStems, as.character)
 df <- data.frame(Question=questions,
                  Option = options, 
                  Type = "radio",
                  stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

 res <- mirtCAT(df)
 res

Unless you are referring to other package in the interface, but these also will accept similar definitions (e.g., lastpage() is a function called to generate the last page in its entirety). 

Re: final_fun() is called just before the last page has been rendered (it's used for saving and such, so on the off chance the last page crashes at least the results would save correctly). 

Phil

parts:
For the redirect portion, I think just defining the final_page input to include a hyperlink to the website you are trying to direct traffic to would be sufficient. 

Regarding the GET request, that's a bit on the tricky side. Ideally I do not want to expose the server.R function to front end users because this interface must be highly controlled for CAT sessions to work properly (as opposed to more general shiny applications). I suppose some question are in order to determine how to control this behaviour:

1) Would this GET request be initialized at runtime, or must this be updated throughout the CAT session? 
2) Could this GET call be avoided if in the initial script the fetching occurred and were simply passed to mirtCAT as user-define custom variable to be accessed when needed?
3) What is the end goal here, how do you plan on using this ID variable index in your application? 

I think if I understood the end-goal of what you're trying to go for I'd know better how to accommodate the request. Sorry if that's a pain.

Phil

Hi Phil,

thanks for getting back at this!
So in my case (obviously I can't speak for Felix), participants first work with another shiny app. Once they are done with that app, they are being forwarded to mirtCAT. Both, app#1 and mirtCAT store data about the participants and it would be highly interesting for me to combine data of both apps. Currently, participants have to enter a pseudonym in both apps so that I can link the data manually. This is problematic because a) participants appear not to remember the pseudonym they used in app#1 and b) participants have to enter the pseudonym twice (which is not so comfortable).
I would thus like app#1 to forward to mirtCAT with a link like www.my-mir-cat.com/?id=1234567 and mirtCAT to store this string (e.g., person$url) , so that I can save it alongside the person data from mirtCAT.

2) If I understand this correctly, I would say yes (see also the link I provided in my first post).
